item.title: Alanis Morissette, Michael Bublé & More Launch Canada’s 2026 World Cup Opening Ceremony
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we're diving into the latest news from the music world and beyond. I'm your host, and today we're talking about the star-studded opening ceremony of the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Canada.
[Music transitions to a lively tune]
Host: The ceremony took place on Friday, June 12th, at Toronto Stadium, and it was a night to remember. Alessia Cara kicked things off with a spirited performance of her hit song "Wild Things," singing from inside a giant gold-outlined soccer ball. The opening number also featured dancers waving flags and carrying artwork inspired by Canadian wildlife.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of "Wild Things"]
Host: The ceremony continued with performances by Nora Fatehi, DJ Sanjoy, and rapper Vegedream, who performed their track "Siir" from the official FIFA World Cup 2026 album. Elyanna and Jessie Reyez also took the stage to perform another song from the project, "Illuminate."
[Music transitions to a brief clip of "Siir" or "Illuminate"]
Host: But one of the most memorable moments of the night came when Alanis Morissette delivered a stirring rendition of the Canadian national anthem, "O Canada." The audience was also treated to a performance of the national anthem of Bosnia and Herzegovina by violinist Aleksandar Gajić.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of "O Canada"]
Host: And to close out the ceremony, Michael Bublé took the stage alongside the Sole Power Choir to perform a rendition of Sam Cooke's "Bring It on Home to Me." It was a night that truly showcased Canada's identity and energy, and set the stage for an exciting tournament.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of "Bring It on Home to Me"]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you next time.
[Outro music plays]
